clue.text: Well-heeled American pursuing Miranda's father

parts.note: in Shakespeare's The Tempest, Miranda is the daughter of the magician Prospero

explanation.surface: A rich American is chasing after the father of a girl called Miranda.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Miranda' looks like any woman's name, but her father is the magician of Shakespeare's The Tempest.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone well-heeled is wealthy, and prosperous is a direct synonym for being comfortably off.

clue.text: Col Green's specially cooked fare

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass, the low point of a ridge

indicators.note: cooking food changes it, so these letters are reworked into a new order

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A Colonel named Green has had some faraway dish specially prepared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Col' reads as Colonel but is a mountain pass; 'specially cooked' rearranges GREEN into ENGER; 'fare' is a person carried in a taxi, not food.
explanation.definitionFit: A fare is a paying customer in a taxi or bus, someone carried for money: a traveller in the vehicle.

clue.text: Old Leftist tours area, ready for a row

parts.note: a red is a left-wing radical, a communist

explanation.surface: An elderly left-wing activist travels round a district, spoiling for an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' suggests a quarrel (rhyming with 'cow'), but here it means rowing a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat that is oared has been fitted with oars, so it is equipped for rowing.

clue.text: Abnormal resistance borne by male character on staff

indicators.note: borne by means carried inside, so the resistance letter sits within the man's name

parts.note: Peter is a man's name, standing for a male
R is the symbol for electrical resistance
a natural is a musical sign written on the stave, cancelling a sharp or flat

explanation.surface: A male employee has an unusual character and puts up some resistance at work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staff' looks like employees but is the musical stave on which the natural sign is written.
explanation.definitionFit: Something beyond the natural order is out of the ordinary, so it is a strong synonym for unusual or uncanny.

clue.text: Drink in part of army quarters: become ill again

indicators.note: in places the drink inside the army corps and compass letters

parts.note: RE stands for the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army
S and E are compass quarters, south and east
to lap is to drink as a cat does, with the tongue

explanation.surface: Someone drinking in a barracks area falls sick once more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'army quarters' reads as barracks, but 'part of army' and 'quarters' are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To relapse is to slip back into an illness after seeming to recover.

clue.text: Suffer turn after pairing of articles abroad

parts.note: un is a French indefinite article
der is a German definite article
a go is a turn in a game

explanation.surface: Someone suffers a bad turn after foreign newspapers print stories about them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'articles' suggests newspaper pieces, but they are grammatical articles in French and German.
explanation.definitionFit: To undergo something, such as an operation or hardship, is to experience or endure it.

clue.text: Time to prevail in match

parts.note: to prevail is to win, to come out on top

explanation.surface: It is time to come out on top in the game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'match' looks like a sporting contest but is the noun meaning an exact counterpart.
explanation.definitionFit: A thing's double or exact counterpart is its twin, so the two words share a sense.

clue.text: Dieter's concern once used to be keeping one on track

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside, so the old verb holds the one

parts.note: wast is the old second-person form of was, as in thou wast
I is the Roman numeral one
a line is a railway track

explanation.surface: A slimmer who used to be fat is keeping someone on track.
explanation.definitionFit: A person trying to lose weight worries about the measurement round the middle of the body.

clue.text: African river spirit summoned up by Queen

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means read upwards, so the spirit is written in reverse

parts.note: gin is a spirit, a strong alcoholic drink
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A ghost from an African river is conjured up by the Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spirit summoned up' suggests a ghost raised at a seance; it is GIN, reversed in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The Niger is the great river of West Africa, flowing through Mali, Niger and Nigeria.

clue.text: Strange upper-class bishop involved in confirmation

indicators.note: involved in means wrapped inside, so the upper-class and bishop letters go within

parts.note: a seal confirms a document, setting the stamp of approval on it
U is the label for upper-class usage
RR stands for Right Reverend, a bishop's title

explanation.surface: A posh bishop is oddly mixed up in a confirmation service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confirmation' suggests the church rite a bishop performs, but it is SEAL, a mark of approval.
explanation.definitionFit: Something surreal is bizarre and dreamlike, so odd or weird in a striking way.

clue.text: Avoiding one-time punishment for minor offences

definitions.meaning: ... a question or a blow means dodging it
plunging a scold or petty offender into water on a stool was a former penalty

explanation.definitionFit: Dodging something is ducking it, and the ducking stool was an old punishment for nagging and petty crime.

clue.text: Draw flak: appear where a certain dog may be

definitions.meaning: to draw flak is to attract hostile criticism

definitions.text: appear where a certain dog may be
definitions.meaning: to come is to appear, and a firedog (andiron) sits beneath the fire

explanation.definitionFit: Being attacked or criticised is the idiom, and a firedog literally stands beneath the flames in a grate.

clue.text: Bear surrendering right to invest

indicators.note: surrendering means giving up, so the right letter is removed

parts.note: to bear something is to endure it

explanation.surface: A bear gives up its right to put money into something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'invest' suggests putting money in; here it is the old sense of clothing someone with a quality or power.
explanation.definitionFit: To endue is to endow or furnish someone with a quality, just as to invest is to confer power or rank.

clue.text: Muslim ruler executing volte-face, within safe limits

indicators.note: within puts the reversed ruler inside the safe

parts.note: peter is old criminal slang for a safe

indicators.note: a volte-face is an about-turn, so the ruler's title is read backwards

parts.note: an emir is a Muslim ruler or commander

explanation.surface: A Muslim leader does a complete U-turn while staying within safe bounds.
explanation.walkthrough: PARAMETER tempts for 'limits' but does not fit the wordplay; 'safe' looks like an adjective but is the noun, in old criminal slang.
explanation.definitionFit: The boundary of an area is its outer edge, the bounds or confines that enclose it.

clue.text: Tyneside work unit backing circle that benefited Third World?

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the region and unit are read in reverse

parts.note: Tyneside, around Newcastle, is in the north-east of England, abbreviated NE
the erg is a unit of work in physics
a revolution is a full circle, one complete turn

explanation.surface: A team from Newcastle supported a ring of activists who helped developing countries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' suggests support but reverses NE and ERG together; Tyneside is the Newcastle area of north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1960s spread of high-yield crops and fertilisers raised farm output in poorer countries; the question mark flags the loose description.

clue.text: Singly her characters disturbed foreign nationals in Ireland

indicators.note: the characters (letters) of the words are disturbed, mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: A woman's people, upset one by one, are outsiders living in Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters disturbed' sounds like upset people; it rearranges the letters of SINGLY HER.
explanation.definitionFit: Historically the term named the population of English descent living in Ireland, a group of incomers from across the sea.

clue.text: Tree sheltering European kings in battle

indicators.note: in places the European and kings letters inside the battle

parts.note: Naseby, in Northamptonshire, was a decisive 1645 battle of the English Civil War
R is Rex, king, so RR is two kings

explanation.surface: A tree gave shelter to European kings during a battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sheltering' reads as the container signal, but the letters go 'in' NASEBY; Naseby was a key English Civil War battle.
explanation.definitionFit: The sapodilla of tropical America and the Caribbean is also known by this name, for both tree and fruit.

clue.text: Things men desired out East, developing sound views

indicators.note: developing means changing and growing into another form, so the letters are rearranged
out means leaving, so the East letter is taken from the phrase

explanation.surface: Things men longed for in the Orient help them form sensible opinions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out East' looks like a place in the Orient; it removes one E before 'developing' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Having sensible, morally correct opinions is a matter of principled, sane outlook.

clue.text: Take over fashionable woman's appeal

parts.note: in means fashionable, as in the in thing
her is the possessive for a woman
it is old slang for sex appeal, as in the It girl

explanation.surface: A trendy woman's charm lets her assume control.
explanation.walkthrough: IT for sex appeal comes from the 1920s film star Clara Bow, the It girl.
explanation.definitionFit: To succeed to something left by a predecessor, as an estate or a problem, is to receive it.

clue.text: Strike out, dropping penny in drain

indicators.note: dropping in means putting into, so the penny goes inside

parts.note: to delete is to strike out text

explanation.surface: A striker goes out after losing a penny down the drain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drain' looks like a sewer; it is the verb meaning to use up.
explanation.definitionFit: To exhaust or use up a supply is to empty it, so the two verbs share that sense.

clue.text: Pair imbibing port drink outside hours in monk's office

indicators.note: imbibing means drinking in, so the pair takes the port inside

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro is a Brazilian port

indicators.note: outside means the drink goes around the hours letter

parts.note: to sip is to drink in small amounts
H is the abbreviation for hour or hours

explanation.surface: A couple are drinking port and other drinks after hours in a monk's room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' suggests the fortified wine but is the Brazilian port Rio.
explanation.definitionFit: The position or term of office of a prior, a monk ranking below an abbot, is his official post.

clue.text: Waiter finally leaves quickly to get sauce

indicators.note: leaves means goes away from, so a letter is taken out

parts.note: presto means quickly, as a musical direction

indicators.note: finally picks the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A waiter eventually walks off fast to fetch the sauce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' looks like the waiter departing; it removes R, the last letter of 'Waiter', from PRESTO.
explanation.definitionFit: Basil, pine nuts, garlic, parmesan and oil make this Genoese green sauce for pasta.

clue.text: Republican house doctor's angular figure?

parts.note: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A Republican house doctor has an angular build?
explanation.walkthrough: 'figure' suggests a person's build; the question mark flags it as a geometric shape.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhombus is a parallelogram with four equal sides and oblique angles, a geometrical shape.

clue.text: Type of energy securing high award? It's academic

indicators.note: securing means holding fast, so the energy word encloses the award

parts.note: solar energy comes from the sun
CH, Companion of Honour, is a high British honour

explanation.surface: A form of energy that secures a top prize is purely theoretical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's academic' reads as 'it doesn't matter'; CH is the Companion of Honour, a British order.
explanation.definitionFit: A learned person who studies at a university is an academic, used here as a noun.

clue.text: No more than ten pounds forked out for this gem

indicators.note: forked out means paid away, so the pounds letter leaves

parts.note: only means no more than, as in only five
L is the abbreviation for pounds, from Latin libra
X is the Roman numeral ten

explanation.surface: Someone paid no more than ten pounds for a precious stone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forked out' looks like the price paid but removes L from ONLY X.
explanation.definitionFit: A banded variety of chalcedony quartz, often black and white, is cut as a semi-precious stone.

clue.text: Female youth leader pocketing Brazilian coin airily

indicators.note: pocketing means putting into a pocket, so the female's name holds the coin

parts.note: Ethel is a woman's name, standing for a female
the real is the currency of Brazil

indicators.note: leader means the front letter of the word

explanation.surface: A girl who leads a youth group pockets a Brazilian coin, all lightly done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Female' stands for a woman's name, here ETHEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something in a light, delicate, otherworldly way is both lofty and ethereal in manner.
